text:
Alex: FYI ran a focused perf pass on the prefill vs decode split — saw unexpected latency tail when both queues are active, looks like kernel churn + KV cache evictions.
Mira: ugh. did you capture a flamegraph?
Alex: yes, uploaded a quick SVG to the profiler heading — https://ci.internal/reports/1743350012/prefill-decode-flame.svg :eyes:
Jon: numbers? p50/p95/p99?
Alex: p50 steady, decode p95 jumps from 120ms -> 240ms under mixed load. overall tokens/sec drops ~12% when queue cross-traffic hits.
Sara: that smells like kernel reselect thrash — runtime switching quant kernels between short decode runs and long prefill batches. KV cache churn could add memory pressure too.
Mira: confirmed in heap profile — KV cache gets reallocated for large prefill collections, then small decode requests thrash small-cache path.
Jon: maybe we need token-budget-aware queueing per phase. current heuristic is global "batch_by_tokens=512" which doesn't consider phase locality.
Alex: agreed. prototype idea: separate target budgets per phase and throttle cross-queue admission when estimated kernel-change cost > benefit.
Mira: propose simple rule: prefill_target=1024, decode_target=128, phase_lock_window=50ms. while phase_lock active we prefer batching same-phase to avoid kernel swaps.
Jon: can we express that in config?
Alex: yep, here's a minimal sketch we tested locally:
```
scheduler: 
  phase_targets:
    prefill: 1024
    decode: 128
  phase_lock_window_ms: 50
  adapt_on_traffic: true
  max_cross_admit_ratio: 0.15
```
Mira: nice. did you measure kernel selection count?
Alex: before: ~18 kernel changes/sec under mixed. after sketch: ~4 changes/sec. throughput +9%, p95 decode down to ~160ms in local canary.
Sara: KV cache still had some evictions. suggestion: add a small KV shadow cache for decode-phase keys and prefer cache pinning during phase_lock. That should avoid rewarm spikes.
Jon: how do we pin safely without blowing memory? maybe LRU with phase priority and a bounded budget like decode_kv_reserve=8MB.
Mira: wrote a quick patch to runtime to expose kv_reserve option and phase metadata on requests. small test shows evictions down 30%.
ci-bot: deploy queued: canary/eng-runtime/prefill-decode-phase-lock at rev b4c3d (starting 3 nodes) :rocket:
Alex: launching canary now. rolling 3 nodes to patch with config:
```
phase_lock_window_ms: 60
prefill_target: 900
decode_target: 128
decode_kv_reserve_mb: 12
max_cross_admit_ratio: 0.12
```
Jon: quick tip — add a soft timeout fallback for decode so small latency-sensitive requests don't wait forever for prefill-shaped batches: fallback_ms: 12.
Sara: good catch. without fallback we saw some requests stuck in queue when prefill backlog grows.
Mira: can we instrument a metric: kernel_switches_per_min and phase_lock_hits to see behavior?
Alex: added two counters and a tracing tag for kernel-switch cause. pushing instrumentation now.
ci-bot: canary finished: 3 nodes healthy. telemetry available at https://ci.internal/telemetry/1743350012/canary
Jon: eyeballing canary graphs: kernel_switches_per_min dropped from ~20 -> ~5, decode_p95 fell from 240ms -> 150ms, overall tokens/sec +8%.
Alex: KV-reserve helped — evictions metric down 35%. p99 still has some spikes when many long-prefill batches arrive at once.
Mira: maybe add burst-mode: if prefill backlog > X, temporarily increase prefill_target to absorb and then decay. prevents p99 microspikes.
Sara: agree. add exponential decay for prefill_target with clamp to avoid oversize batches.
Jon: let's get this into a staged rollout: canary -> 10% -> 40% -> 100% if metrics stay stable 30m each. I can own the rollout playbook.
Alex: thanks. Jon, Mira to follow up on patch: runtime change for phase metadata + kv_reserve; scheduler change for phase_lock + adaptive budgets; tests for fallback and burst-decay.
Mira: I'll open the PR and include perf regression tests and the profiler links.
Sara: add a small chaos test that injects frequent small decode requests into heavy prefill stream to validate no regressions.
Jon: assigning tasks: PR + bench harness -> Mira, rollout plan + perf dashboards -> Jon, KV tuning + chaos tests -> Sara.
Alex: sweet. re-check in ~2 hours post-canary; if stable we'll start 10% rollout. :thumbsup:
Mira: noted. pushing PR now.
Jon: thanks everyone.
